stages.name: The loading bay
text: Pallets by the door. Boring stuff. Boring stuff sells.
A ramp, a stack shrink-wrapped and ready to ship, and a bay door somebody left on the latch for a smoke break they're still on.
Cages of returns waiting to be checked back in — half of it never faulty, all of it already paid for once by somebody else.
fail_text: Headlights swing across the yard. You're behind a pallet before you've decided to be.
The bay door drops on its timer and the crash brings a torch round the corner of the building.
The smoke break ends early and there's a hi-vis stood between you and the ramp asking who you're with.

stages.name: The floor
text: Rows of it. You could be here all night. You've got eleven minutes.
Aisles taller than the forklift, a scanner gun on a charging dock, and a system that won't miss any of this until a rep reorders next month.
The good aisle's the one with the anti-theft tape on the shelf edges, which is the warehouse telling you exactly where to look.
fail_text: A forklift you didn't clock has a driver you didn't clock. You leave the trolley.
You take the wrong aisle and it's the one under the only working camera on the night rotation.
The scanner gun you moved was logged in, and a supervisor's tablet is now asking why it's walking to the door.

stages.name: The cage
text: Locked mesh. Whatever's in a cage in a warehouse is worth caging.
A steel cage inside the building, its own padlock, the small dear stock kept where the agency staff can't reach — which is nearly where you can't either.
The cage is where the phones and the perfume live, and there's a key card reader on it, and a lad on nights whose card it is and whose nerve it isn't.
fail_text: The bolt cutters slip and the noise carries. Somewhere a dog decides it cares.
The mesh is alarmed on a contact you cut, and cutting it is the same as ringing a bell.
The lad's card was deactivated this afternoon because his nerve turned into a confession, and the cage doesn't open.

stages.name: The office
text: Petty cash tin, a laptop, and the shift rota — which tells you when to come back.
A mezzanine office over the floor, a safe under the desk, and a whiteboard with the delivery schedule that's worth more than the cash to a man who plans.
Manager's office, a fob on a hook, a monitor still logged in, and the loss-prevention reports open on it telling you exactly what they've noticed and haven't.
fail_text: Silent alarm. You learn it was silent when the yard lights all come on at once.
The office window looks straight down the floor and a nightshift picker looks straight back up at it.
The logged-in monitor was logged in because someone's still on shift, and they've just come back for their brew.

stages.name: The cold store
text: Nobody puts a padlock on a fridge for fun.
A walk-in chiller stacked with premium meat that's worth a caterer's fortune and worth nothing at all if you're slow enough to let it thaw.
The cold store hums louder than the rest of the building, which is the sound of something being kept at exactly the temperature that means it's dear.
fail_text: The door swings shut behind you and the handle's the kind that only opens from outside.
Propping the chiller door tells a monitoring firm the freezer's failing, and a monitoring firm tells someone with keys.
The cold slows you down more than you costed for, and your breath's fogging on the camera by the time you find the good pallet.
